name: St. Regis Aruba Resort
positioning: The St. Regis Aruba Resort, at the south end of Palm Beach in Aruba, home to the first St. Regis casino
best_for: Families who want a kids program, a children's pool and multi-bedroom suites
Travelers who enjoy St. Regis rituals like afternoon tea and champagne sabering
Guests who want butler service whatever room they book

facts.text: The resort is positioned at the south end of Palm Beach.
Akira Back is a rooftop restaurant helmed by its namesake chef.
Akira Back is a tribute to steak and sushi.
Nuba's dishes are inspired by Aruba's heritage of Salt and Rum.
Afternoon tea at The St. Regis Bar is served in Ginori 1735 porcelain.
A champagne sabering ceremony is held daily on the St. Regis Bar Terrace.
The St. Regis Spa's private treatment rooms feature Sothys Paris products.
Guests of all room categories have access to the St. Regis Butler Service.
The suites include Two- and Three-Bedroom Suites, ideal for families and extended stays.
The Family Traditions program includes Family Yoga, Memory Journals and Cultural Storytelling.
The outdoor pools include a children's pool.

highlights.text: The resort's casino is the first-ever St. Regis casino.
The Bon Bini Mary is named for the Papiamento phrase for welcome and blends locally sourced papaya, fresh lime and habanero chili.
Guests in the John Jacob Astor and Caroline Suites get private airport transfers, a dedicated butler and daily access to a reserved pool or beach cabana.
Guests can charge dining at some venues of the neighboring Ritz-Carlton, Aruba to their room.
Because the resort sits on the western side of the island, the water is quite calm, even during the windier months.

considerations.text: The hotel does not provide a shuttle service; Queen Beatrix International Airport is approximately 7 miles away.
The minimum age to check in is 18.
